# tkmt-lab — research lab of Tatsuhiko Takimoto

> Independent research in mathematics and science with AI teams. The first results are on fullerene graphs; later work covers Bell inequalities, analogue Hawking radiation, epidemic-model identifiability, Heesch numbers of polyforms and term-minimal chemical rate equations. Each paper is released with a Lean 4 formalization where available, verification data, and a machine-readable claim list stating what has and has not been checked. Checked data sets and tools released without a paper are listed under Data & tools.

## Works

- [Catalog of results (JSON)](https://tkmt-lab.github.io/catalog.json): every published work and claim in one file — stable claim ids, evidence kinds (Lean declarations and axioms, Comparator, independent implementation, AI review, finite computation, numerical evidence, and statement correspondence that does not establish truth), verification commands, DOIs and what is not claimed. Schema: https://tkmt-lab.github.io/catalog.schema.json; explanation: https://tkmt-lab.github.io/catalog.html. Start there, then read the repository's AGENTS.md and run its checks.
- [How the work is checked](https://tkmt-lab.github.io/verification.html): eight reusable verification procedures (frozen statements and Comparator, Lean axiom gates, separately written implementations, certificate checkers, separate AI readers, scope audits, machine-readable claims, correction records), each with what it establishes, what remains, and an example pinned to a published commit. Japanese: https://tkmt-lab.github.io/ja/verification.html.
- [A3 classification of linear gSW paths](https://github.com/tkmt-lab/a3-gsw-classification): GC(k,l)[C20] has a literal linear generalized Stone-Wales path iff an explicit two-stage residue criterion holds. Proved in Lean 4 (standard axioms only), checked with Comparator against an independent statement. Start with AGENTS.md; evidence in packet/claims.json. Current release: tag v1.1.0; commit 58124b20fa4a3b19aaa62e734c2036210f7bdcf8; version DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23515012; concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23491202 (all versions).
- [Eventual periodicity on affine rays](https://github.com/tkmt-lab/gsw-ray-periodicity): for fullerene families built from a fixed number of convex lattice faces with affine coordinates, existence of a literal gSW path is eventually periodic along every integer affine ray. Main theorem proved in Lean 4 (standard axioms only) for a specification with weaker hypotheses than the paper, checked with Comparator; a prose lemma connects the paper's geometric hypotheses to it. For Graver's family K3(r,s) (two caps of four triangles of side r joined by three hexagons with sides r, r, s, r, r, s) the result on every ray in r, s ≥ 1 and the closed classification (for r, s ≥ 2: a path exists iff s ≡ ±1 mod r) are Lean-proved with no prose step; the same holds for Graver's family C1 (for a, b ≥ 1: a path exists iff b = 1), for Graver's family O2 the ray result and absence of paths for t, d ≥ 2 are Lean-proved with no prose step, and so are the ray result for Graver's family D14 and the classification (r ≥ 2) and ray result for Graver's family E10. For Graver's family D12 the closed classification (for positive r, s: a path exists iff r | s−1, r | s+1 or |r−3s| = 1) and the ray result are Lean-proved (v1.10.0); two earlier computer-assisted proofs are kept as additional evidence. The Lean proof was written with knowledge of those proofs and is not a third independent derivation; no human peer review is claimed. Lean also covers the family arithmetic. Start with AGENTS.md. Current release: tag v1.10.0; commit 8eea5994bfebdcca4865528bd7524af4064f9c16; version DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23589703; concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23491204 (all versions).
- [Bell facet certificates](https://github.com/tkmt-lab/bell-facet-certificates): for the two fixed published lists of C. Staufenbiel — (4,5,2,2) with 49,358 rows and (4,6,2,2) with 4,327,233 rows — every row is a facet of the local polytope, and every row except the single positivity representative of each list is strictly violated by a two-qubit pure state with binary projective measurements given by rational numbers. Two separately written exact verifiers accept every row. Finite evidence concerning Gill's question; no completeness of the lists, optimal quantum values, Lean proof or human peer review is claimed. Full (4,6,2,2) certificates are release attachments. Start with AGENTS.md; claims in claims.json. Current release: tag v1.0.0; commit cd1e141455cf3f5fe05a739782271201cdefe7e8; version DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23538697; concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23538696 (all versions).
- [Dispersive offset of the analogue Hawking temperature](https://github.com/tkmt-lab/hawking-dispersive-offset): for a one-dimensional flow with quartic superluminal dispersion ω² = k² + k⁴/Λ² and a single horizon, the zero-frequency temperature satisfies T(0)/T_H − 1 = κ g‴(0)/(12Λ²) + O(Λ⁻⁴), with the local coefficient b0 = g‴(0)/(12κ) in derivatives of the flow at the horizon. Formal asymptotic calculation under three stated assumptions (not proved, no remainder bound), supported by full scattering numerics, predictions recorded before calculation, and a separately written scattering code (agreement within about 1e-7). No Lean proof or human peer review. `python3 -B reproduce.py` re-runs everything. Start with AGENTS.md; claims in claims.json. Current release: tag v1.0.0; commit 00f229f7afd38ebd67be3daa27f89dcb78436aaf; version DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23553203; concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23553202 (all versions).
- [Global identifiability of a behavioral SIR model](https://github.com/tkmt-lab/behavioral-sir-identifiability): for S' = −βSI/(1+αI)^k, I' = βSI/(1+αI)^k − γI, R' = γI with a fixed known integer k ≥ 2, observed through I(t) with known total population, α, β, γ and S(0), I(0), R(0) are generically globally identifiable — the integer-exponent case of Conjecture 2 of Pant, Saucedo and Pogudin. Prose proof read by two AI reviewers, with exact computer-algebra checks for k = 1..12; no Lean proof or human peer review; non-integer or unknown k and noisy data not covered. Start with AGENTS.md; claims in claims.json. Current release: tag v1.0.0; commit 6691a76801a522592712e41993b6f4353decee88; version DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23553807; concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23553806 (all versions).
- [Heesch number certificates](https://github.com/tkmt-lab/heesch-certificates): for a fixed selection of 3,964 polyominoes, polyhexes and polyiamonds from C. S. Kaplan's tables, every Heesch number (hole-free Hc and outer-holes Hh) equals Kaplan's value and comes with checkable evidence: 6,574 corona witnesses accepted by two geometric checkers (lower bounds) and 5,019 unsatisfiability proofs accepted by drat-trim (upper bounds). Soundness of the SAT encoding on the square, hexagonal and triangular grids is proved in Lean 4 (standard axioms only; Comparator, six kernel runs); the checked CNFs equal the Lean encoding up to renaming by a recorded finite comparison. Also: maximal-corona counts for 22 shapes by two separately written implementations, and a restricted search of 3,442 polyominoes with 20-28 cells that found no finite Hh = 4. The DRAT proofs are checked outside Lean; outer-layer counts have no certificate; the search is not exhaustive; only the listed shapes are covered; no priority or human peer review is claimed. Start with AGENTS.md; claims in claims.json. Current release: tag v1.0.0; commit 271bc8ce223a1fd641494352eb31f350e3d8bf37; version DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23572883; concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23572882 (all versions).

- [Term-minimal quadratic mass-action systems](https://github.com/tkmt-lab/minimal-terms-quadratic-mass-action): Paper 7. For nine invariant-line-type multisets in two-species quadratic mass-action systems, the minimum nonzero component-term counts are 8,8,8,8,8,8,8,6,6. Exact examples attain the bounds and a proof over real nonnegative parameters excludes fewer terms. Five counts improve on the best examples in the source paper; four prior attained bounds are proved optimal in this domain. Reactant molecularity at most two, unrestricted products, a positive equilibrium with zero Jacobian, and nonzero homogeneous resultant; terms are counted in concentration coordinates, separately in each component. A separate verification agrees but shared the specification and mathematical preparation. No minimum reaction count, historical-domain equivalence, priority, Lean proof or human peer review is claimed. Start with AGENTS.md; claims in claims.json. Check with `python3 -B checkers/verify.py`. Current release: tag v1.0.0; commit dfb36e121ec0b014e495abd07f870ea76503fbc4; version DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23602991; concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23602990 (all versions).

- [Twelve two-base-pair helices](https://github.com/tkmt-lab/maxstacks-two-bp-helices): Paper 8. In the fixed maxStacks target family T_D, a 71-base sequence uniquely designs T_12; T_D is undesignable for every D >= 13. GU pairs allowed, no isolated pairs, one-base hairpins and separators in the targets. Finite DP and CNF checks, LRAT certificates accepted by cake_lpr under the documented trust boundary, and prose normalization/general-D arguments are distinct evidence. No proof-assistant verification of the RNA-to-CNF correspondence, classification of every D <= 12, arbitrary RNA-tree result, usual three-base-hairpin or Turner-energy result, experimental RNA, priority or human peer review. Start with AGENTS.md; claim in claims.json. Current release: tag v1.0.0; commit 5e150006317ecaabf4d63150cba46bc04ae7d3ac; version DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23679268; concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23679267 (all versions).

- [A certified three-equilibrium bound for 375 fixed quadratic zero-one reaction networks](https://github.com/tkmt-lab/multistationarity-375-networks-bound): For each network in Tang–Zhang’s fixed 375-network list, at most three distinct positive equilibria at every strictly positive rate vector, including degenerate equilibria. Three species, six reactions, quadratic zero-one complexes and rank three. Exact Cramer certificates (272 cubic, 103 quartic residuals), a historical independent resultant derivation checked by explicit Sylvester determinants, and the article’s proof support the bound. Also includes a post-selected finite structural observation and one seven-reaction family, not general classifications. The list, original upper-bound claim and reported 373/2 stability classification are Tang and Zhang’s; enumeration, all existence witnesses and the 373-network stability classification are not reverified here. No formal verification, human peer review, priority or new blind review during packaging. Start with AGENTS.md; claims in claims.json. Current release: tag v1.0.0; commit cc161da467e90032a4c435bc5bd3e7622f159e81; version DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23715811; concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23715810 (all versions).

## Data & tools

- [Rooted periodic-net identification tests (RCSR, 1-WL)](https://github.com/tkmt-lab/periodic-net-wl-tests): 99 test cases built from a pinned RCSR-content commit, each a pair of nets with a root vertex in each. Each case records r_min, the smallest radius at which the two rooted balls (all vertices within r edges of the root and the edges between them) are not isomorphic, and r_WL, the smallest radius at which stable 1-WL colour refinement, with initial colours (distance from root, degree in ball), separates them. In 97 cases r_WL > r_min; the largest gap is 4 (tsa V1 / tsg V3: r_min = 4, r_WL = 8). A checker separate from the generator verifies a complete root-preserving isomorphism at r_min − 1 and a non-isomorphism certificate at r_min; the 6 core cases were also computed by a separately written implementation, the other 93 only by this package's checker. Bare graphs only: nothing is claimed about methods that use species, coordinates, distances or angles, about GNNs in general, about radii as numbers of layers, or about a maximum over RCSR (the cases are a selection). No RCSR data is redistributed; the code downloads it and checks its SHA-256. No paper, priority, human review or formal proof. Start with AGENTS.md; claims in claims.json. Current release: tag v1.0.0; commit e427857923563e55a9fdb8ba06cb6a5bb953cd85; version DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23587478; concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23587477 (all versions).

- [Counterexamples for Boolean-network variable elimination](https://github.com/tkmt-lab/boolean-reduction-counterexamples): regression inputs for implementations of asynchronous Boolean-network reduction. Three counterexamples (E1, E2, E3) in which eliminating one variable without an essential self-dependency creates a motif-avoidant attractor (MAA): E1 and E3 delete a variable on no directed cycle, and all three satisfy an exploratory mediator-and-monotonicity condition informed by Tonello–Paulevé (arXiv:2406.02304); plus a coordinate-transformed copy of E1 and Examples 7 and 8 of Pastva et al. (arXiv:2410.03976) as controls. Each case has formulas and fixed expected finite dynamics (transitions, attractors, trap spaces, MAAs); the Python checker (standard library) recomputes them exactly, and 16 self-tests include a second algorithm. Saved records of earlier exhaustive enumerations (also with a separate implementation, not blinded to n=3 counts) found no counterexample on 1–3 variables, giving minimum variable count four for each condition; the enumeration is not rerun. The general fact that elimination can create or remove MAAs is known; novelty of these examples is not established; the conditions are this study's exploratory candidates, not theorems of the cited authors. No safety theorem, edge-minimality, biological claim, priority, human review or formal proof. Start with AGENTS.md; claims in claims.json. Current release: tag v1.0.0; commit a782c11e0abf52e9808a50d1a91a9bfdf8c5428f; version DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23636196; concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23636195 (all versions).

## Supporting material for our papers

Not a separate result: the main theorems of three of our published repositories restated in Lean.

- [Lean statements from published papers](https://github.com/tkmt-lab/lean-statements): 9 Lean files containing 18 theorem statements from 3 published repositories (a3-gsw-classification, gsw-ray-periodicity and heesch-certificates). For readers and programs that want to inspect assumptions, import one statement or find its proof. Definitions, namespaces, hypotheses and types are preserved; every theorem body is intentionally by sorry. Each formal_proof attribute links to a proof at a fixed public commit; research solved marks status. Recorded checks compare the original and local theorem types and inspect metadata. Building this package does not establish mathematical truth or execute the linked proofs. Files with repeated namespaces must be used separately. Not an official part of formal-conjectures and not contributed to it; compatibility with its Lean version and full linter suite is unverified. No new proof or human expert review. Start with AGENTS.md; claims and per-declaration scopes in claims.json. Current release: tag v1.0.0; commit b3647ee21a1fd572e8a500f2288921116dbb098d; version DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23594152; concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23594151 (all versions).

- [Stability certificates for two exceptional reaction networks](https://github.com/tkmt-lab/exception-networks-stability-certificates): Data and tools for steady-state and stability calculations on the two Tang–Zhang Example 4 networks. Three fixed rational rate vectors have nine certified positive equilibria, three exponentially stable in total. Two written derivations give the all-positive-rate bounds; two implementations recompute the fixed certificates. Not a general-purpose solver, new classification or novelty claim. No proof-assistant verification or human peer review; not blind testing. Current release: tag v1.0.0; commit 1981c553152bae7fe76f23704fda5c06fd354a7e; version DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23659209; concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23659208 (all versions).

## Built on

- The question: linear generalized Stone–Wales paths as defined by A. Bille, V. Buchstaber and E. Spodarev ("Some open mathematical problems on fullerenes", 2024/2025).
- The Goldberg–Coxeter construction (named after M. Goldberg and H. S. M. Coxeter; developed for plane graphs, with zigzag theory, by M. Dutour Sikirić and M. Deza).
- J. E. Graver's catalogue of fullerenes with ten or more symmetries; K. Kutnar and D. Marušič on cyclic edge-connectivity of fullerenes.
- The Büchi–Elgot–Trakhtenbrot theorem (monadic second-order logic on words and finite automata).
- For the Bell work: R. Gill's question (Problem 26.B in Krüger–Werner's collection), C. Staufenbiel's sampled facet lists and tools, and S. Lörwald and G. Reinelt's PANDA.
- For the Hawking work: the dispersive analogue-gravity literature, in particular S. Corley and T. Jacobson; W. G. Unruh and R. Schützhold; J. Macher, A. Coutant, S. Finazzi and R. Parentani; U. Leonhardt and S. Robertson; and F. Del Porro, S. Liberati and M. Schneider's effective-horizon result.
- For the epidemic-model work: B. Pant, O. Saucedo and G. Pogudin's question and conjecture; A. Ovchinnikov, G. Pogudin and P. Thompson, and H. Hong, A. Ovchinnikov, G. Pogudin and C. Yap on differential-algebraic identifiability.
- For the Heesch work: H. Heesch's problem; C. S. Kaplan's Heesch numbers of unmarked polyforms, its SAT formulation, dataset and heesch-sat software; C. Mann's survey and C. Mann and B. C. Thomas's computations; A. Fontaine's and B. Bašić's constructions; the Layr-Labs/Eigen Heesch challenge; drat-trim, CaDiCaL, Lingeling, Glucose, PySAT and C. Sinz's sequential counter; C. Codel, J. Avigad and M. Heule's verified SAT encodings.
- For the periodic-net tests: the RCSR database (M. O'Keeffe, M. A. Peskov, S. J. Ramsden and O. M. Yaghi) and the researchers who first described each net; V. A. Blatov and D. M. Proserpio on comparing nets by growing coordination shells; S. N. Pozdnyakov and M. Ceriotti on WL counterexamples for point clouds; O. Delgado-Friedrichs's Gavrog space-group table.
- For the statement collection: the Formal Conjectures Authors, whose file format and category, subject and proof-link attributes it uses (https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/tree/9833012f66a47cdd3a6f3eca9cb4b84e0f18a003).
- For the quadratic mass-action work: N. Yeung and R. Erban, whose classification and term-reduction question are the starting point; L. S. Lyagina and T. A. Newton, whose classification and invariant-line descriptions provide the geometric framework.
- For the two-network certificates and the 375-network bound: Xiaoxian Tang and Jiandong Zhang supplied the fixed list, the two exceptional networks, the upper-bound claim, the reported 373/2 stability classification and the determinant criterion. Angélica Torres and Elisenda Feliu developed determinant reduction and stability-alternation results; Murad Banaji and Elisenda Feliu studied the geometry and bounds of positive equilibria; Murad Banaji and Casian Pantea proved inheritance results for nondegenerate multistationarity.
- Lean 4, mathlib, Comparator and independent Lean kernels.
- Full citations are in each paper or repository.

- Théo Boury, Laurent Bulteau and Yann Ponty for the maxStacks framework and question; the DRAT-trim and CakeML/cake_lpr contributors for certificate checking.

## Other work

- Novelist: Tatsuhiko Takimoto (滝本竜彦), https://tatsuhikotakimoto.com/en/

## Evidence conventions

- Formal proof, independent derivation, AI review, and finite computation are labelled separately in each claims.json.
- Human peer review and novelty are not claimed unless stated.
- Contact: research@tatsuhikotakimoto.com, or GitHub issues in the relevant repository.
- News and the lab diary: https://x.com/tkmt_lab
- Licence of this site's text: CC BY 4.0. Each repository states its own licences.

## Reading partial evidence and missing fields

Use https://tkmt-lab.github.io/catalog-index.json to choose a claim, then read the full catalog entry and its work-level scope and exclusions. The index omits proof types but does not replace them. A null index status means the source has no status label; it is not a mathematical verdict. Evidence kinds do not necessarily establish every clause of a claim. For A3 cor:rays, threshold/period existence is Lean-proved; a certified computing algorithm is not provided. A statement-only entry with an intentional by sorry is not a proof executed by that package. Execution flags such as fresh_lean_run describe their source record, not all historical runs. A documented expected_output is an example to compare with, not a new replay receipt.
